## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Avassutāavassutassa* ("Receiving food with lust") is the fifth *saṅghādisesa* training rule for nuns in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that a lustful nun who receives food from a lustful man incurs an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide transmission of this rule across Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. In Pāli, corresponding rules appear in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Ss 5) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Ss 5) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels across other early Buddhist schools include the Dharmaguptaka (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 8), Mahīśāsaka (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 8), Sarvāstivāda (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 4), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 4 in both Chinese and Tibetan versions), Mahāsaṅghika (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 11), and the Lokottaravāda (*saṅghāvaśeṣa* 11 in Sanskrit) [SuttaCentral].
